extracted.intended_audience: State agency staff, agency counsel, or rulemaking officers preparing New York State rulemaking notices and filings (SAPA/DOS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required standards for preparing, formatting, filing, revising, withdrawing, and adopting New York State rulemaking notices, attachments (RIS/RFA/RAFA/JIS), certifications, and text for publication and E-filing with the Department of State under SAPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment file format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments required by the notice form (e.g., full text, summaries, RIS, RFA, RAFA, JIS, Assessments of Public Comment) must be submitted in MS Word format, not PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After selecting the appropriate box in the form (Parts A, B or C), a paperclip icon will appear to attach your MS Word document. This note is repeated for RIS, RFA, RAFA, JIS and Revised attachments: 'Note: All attachments must be in MS Word - NOT pdf.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (RFA) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rule is subject to RFA requirements, or if an exemption is claimed because the rule will not impose adverse economic impacts on small businesses, you must attach the appropriate RFA or a statement explaining the finding and the reasons upon which the finding was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate box in Part C if the rule is subject to a previously published consolidated RFA or is exempt under SAPA §102(2)(a)(ii) or consensus rulemaking. When a statement/attachment is required a paperclip appears; attach the MS Word file. Where the finding is not readily apparent, the statement must include a summary of the information and methodology underlying the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural Area Flexibility Analysis (RAFA) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: RAFA requirements largely mirror the RFA: if claiming an exemption because the rule will not impose adverse economic impact or reporting/recordkeeping/compliance requirements on rural areas, you must attach a statement explaining the finding and the reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Appendix A for the definition and citation of 'rural areas' for RAFA purposes. After selecting an item in Part A, B or C, if an attachment is required a paperclip shows up to attach the MS Word RAFA statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job Impact Statement (JIS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: JIS requirements differ from RIS/RFA/RAFA; Part B is used to show whether the attachment is full text, summary, or Consolidated JIS and to state whether the rule will have a substantial adverse effect on jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you conclude the rule will not have a substantial adverse effect on jobs you must attach a statement explaining your finding and, except where it is readily apparent, include a summary of the information and methodology underlying the determination. A JIS/Request for Assistance may be attached in lieu of a full JIS. JIS is not required for submissions by the State Comptroller or Attorney General. Attachments must be MS Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting form boxes triggers attachments and consolidated references
rubrics_metrics.description: You must select the appropriate boxes in Parts A, B or C to indicate whether a statement or consolidated prior statement applies (e.g., consolidated RFA/JIS) and provide ID/issue information when referring to a previously published consolidated statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After selecting an item, a yellow paperclip will appear to attach the required MS Word file. For consolidated prior statements you must specify the ID number and issue date of the prior proposal that included the original consolidated statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Certification completion and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency Certification at the end of every State Register notice form must be completed by the person who prepared the form (not by the agency head unless they prepared it), certifying that the preparer has reviewed the form and that information is correct to the best of their knowledge and complies with SAPA and DOS requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you complete the form click the Validate button; correct any deficiencies and re-validate. Once 'verified ok', save the form and upload (E-file) to the West Data Capture System. The certification signals the preparer’s review of appropriate SAPA and Department of State requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Validate button and E-filing acknowledgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Validate button on the form to check for completeness (a message will indicate verified ok or deficiencies). E-filing generates two acknowledgments: an automatic West Data Capture System email and a processing acknowledgment from DAR containing the proposal ID and NYCRR citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The automatic West Data Capture message (sent immediately after upload) is critical to confirm whether E-filing succeeded; DAR is not notified of E-filing failures. After the form verifies ok and is saved, follow DOS e-file instructions to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual instructions for showing deletions and additions in text
rubrics_metrics.description: All text attachments (rules, statements, full text or summary) must include visual instructions showing material deleted and material added: bracket words to be deleted and underline new material to be added. No strikethroughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adding long new text (multi-page Parts, subdivisions, sections) you may instead use a written instruction such as 'A new ... is added to read as follows:' and provide the new text without underlining. For amendments use brackets for deletions and underline new text, and include a written label indicating the type and location of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript-style format requirement (double-spaced, unjustified, indent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare submissions in manuscript style: double-spaced, unjustified text (flush left, ragged right), with a five-character indent for each new paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use boldface text or elaborate header/indent structures — keep plain manuscript formatting. Unreadable or overly-formatted submissions can be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper, print and typeface specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain, flat 8½" x 11" white paper for printed originals and print on a laser printer if submitting a printed original. Use a common proportional-space typeface in 10 or 12 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serif (Times/Times New Roman) or sans serif (Helvetica/Arial) acceptable; avoid single-space/typewriter fonts (Courier). Never use novelty typefaces (script/outline), never use boldface for subheads or emphasis, and use only one typeface for the entire notice and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margin and tab stop requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Set narrow margins and one indent (tab stop) set 5 characters from the left margin; top and bottom margins 1", left and right margins ½", first and only tab stop 5 characters from the left margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these precise measurements to avoid scanning/coding problems that result from textured paper or unusual layouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit only text being amended (avoid sending entire parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only submit the specific text being amended — do not resend a whole Part or section to change a single section or subdivision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including extra text risks unintentional adoption of language that was accidentally omitted or inserted; when repealing an entire section, a simple statement (e.g., 'Section X is repealed') suffices — do not bracket and retype deleted text for an entire section or subdivision being repealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to label and type a lengthy new-text insert
rubrics_metrics.description: When inserting multi-page new text use a written instruction indicating the new text follows (e.g., 'A new section X is added to read as follows:') followed by the new text ununderlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No underlining is needed when the written instruction notifies the reader that new text follows. Use this method for multi-page new Parts, subdivisions and sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to label and type an amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending, label the action (e.g., 'Section X is amended to read as follows:') and show deleted material in brackets and new text underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label your action and indicate the location in the text. Use computer format features to bracket and underline; include written instructions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renumbering rules and cross-reference updating
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding items that require reordering, renumber existing items before adding a new item (i.e., renumber existing (a) and (b) to (b) and (c) then add new (a)). Update all internal cross-references when you renumber or repeal parts/sections/subdivisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is unnecessary to type the text of a renumbered item unless you are also amending it. Warning: failing to update cross-references can create confusion or incorrect rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to repeal versus amend or repeal-and-add
rubrics_metrics.description: If changes are dramatic and widespread, repeal the entire Part and add a new Part; if changes are minor (only one or two sections), avoid repealing and retyping entire long Parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retyping an entire Part to amend one or two sections increases risk of unintended changes, blurs continuity, and creates unnecessary work. Conversely, when many amendments make bracketing/underlining hard to follow, repeal the entire Part and replace it with new text (followed by new text not underlined where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summaries required when text exceeds 2,000 words
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Register will not publish the full text of a rule or any statement that exceeds 2,000 words; in those cases you must submit a summary in under 2,000 words for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when submitting a summary for publication, you must have the full text completed and available by the time you submit the rulemaking proposal; full texts of summarized items must be sent to the designated 101-a and 202(6-a) officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to send full text in addition to E-filing
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to E-filing, you must send each '202(6-a)' and '101-a' officer a copy of the notice along with the full text of the rule and the full text of every attachment and any other information required by Executive Law, section 101-a and SAPA section 202(6-a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Appendix D for e-mail and mailing addresses and instructions. E-filing alone does not replace statutory distribution to these officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-filing success confirmation and DAR processing acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive two e-mail acknowledgments: an automatic West Data Capture System acknowledgment immediately after upload, and a second acknowledgment from DAR after processing that includes assigned ID number and NYCRR citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain the automatic acknowledgment to confirm whether the E-filing submission succeeded or failed. DAR is not notified of E-filing failures; so check the automatic notice and follow up if it indicates failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Register ID number format and action codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Every notice is assigned an alpha-numeric ID code that identifies the agency, issue number, year, serial number and action code (e.g., DOS-01-12-00001-P). Action codes include P (Proposal), RP (Revised Proposal), W (Withdrawal), A (Adoption), E (Emergency Adoption), EP, ERP, EA, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the assigned ID number when submitting revised proposals, emergency adoptions, withdrawals or adoptions. The volume/issue numbering resets annually; the first issue in January is issue one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to publish a Notice of Revised Rule Making for substantial revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you substantially revise the text of a proposed rule after publication, you must submit a Notice of Revised Rule Making to open another public comment period before adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A revised rulemaking is a full proposal and is subject to the same Executive Chamber review as the original proposal. The minimum comment period for a revised proposal is 30 days. If submitted within 90 days of the proposal’s expiration date, the revised notice itself extends the final expiration date an additional 90 days. If the changes affect the original RIS, RFA, RAFA or JIS, you must submit revised versions of those statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'substantial revision'
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantial revision is any addition, deletion, or other change in the text of a proposed rule that materially alters its purpose, meaning, or effect; changes that merely define or clarify text are not substantial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine whether a change is substantial, compare the revised text with the most recently published text. Consult agency counsel for borderline cases. SAPA requires a Notice of Revised Rule Making where changes are substantial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and required items of the Notice of Revised Rule Making form
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Revised Rule Making form largely replicates the Notice of Proposed Rule Making form, but requires special identification of revised RIS/RFA/RAFA/JIS attachments and an Assessment of Public Comment received since the last publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items 1–4: use exact language from the original published proposal unless changed; Item 5: indicate full text or summary; Items 6–8: public hearing/interpreter/accessibility replicate original; Item 9: provide original issue date and ID, list prior revised rulemakings, and identify Parts/sections/subdivisions substantially revised; Items 10–11: contacts; Item 12: public comment minimum 30 days; Items 14–17: attach revised RIS/RFA/RAFA/JIS where necessary and use paperclip to attach MS Word; Item 18: attach Assessment of Public Comment (address only comments received since the last publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Public Comment requirement for revised proposals and adoptions
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing a Notice of Revised Rule Making or when adopting a rule, you must attach an Assessment of Public Comment received since the most recent publication of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not have to reiterate a previously published assessment — you may address only comments received since the last published proposal. Attach the assessment (MS Word) via the form paperclip in Item 18 for revised notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Withdrawal process and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To withdraw a proposal you must E-file a Notice of Withdrawal, identifying the proposal by publication date and ID number, provide the original proposed action and subject as published, state the reasons for withdrawal, and supply contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not need to attach the text of the rule or accompanying statements for a withdrawal, and hard copy submission is no longer necessary. Complete the Validate step and then upload to the West Data Capture System. If you do not affirmatively withdraw, the proposal will remain active until expiration and DAR will publish a Notice of Expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption filing requirements (simultaneous certification and full text)
rubrics_metrics.description: To adopt a rule the agency head (or designated signatory) must sign a certification and file the full text of the rule showing bracketing for deletions and underlining for additions; for State Register publication you must simultaneously submit a Notice of Adoption with required attachments and file the Notice on or before the proposal’s scheduled expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department uses the filed text to update the NYCRR and transmits certification and text to State Archives. Supplements to the NYCRR are issued semi-monthly based on filing dates (1st–15th vs 16th–end of month).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and enforceability of adopted rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Most adopted rules are not effective or enforceable until filed with the Secretary of State with a proper certification and the Notice of Adoption is published in the State Register, with limited exceptions for emergency rules and SAPA §102(2)(a)(ii) rules (e.g., rates, wages, security authorizations) which may be effective upon filing or on a future date specified in the certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely filing: the Notice of Adoption must be filed with DOS on or before the proposal’s expiration date; otherwise adoption may not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content and order of information in a certification
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification (on agency letterhead, titled 'Certification') must state that the rule was duly adopted; name the agency head or designee; give the date of adoption and effective date; and, where applicable, the procedure by which the action was taken and the city of the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional required items: cite statutory authority; if action was not subject to SAPA, cite the statute; for emergency adoptions include specific findings and reasons with factual grounds (paraphrasing SAPA §202 is unacceptable). Also include publication date of the Notice of Proposed Rule Making and dates/manners of any other prior notice required by statute (or state none was required). Sample certifications for agency head, designee, authority/board, and emergency paragraphs are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity required in emergency adoption findings
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting as an emergency measure under SAPA §202, the certification must include the agency’s finding of the need for emergency action and the specific reasons/facts supporting that finding; paraphrasing SAPA §202 is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may submit a separate statement of findings and reasons but it must be accompanied by a signed statement by the agency head certifying that these were the findings made. Emergency adoptions are effective immediately upon filing when justified, and special permanent emergency codes exist for certain §102(2)(a)(ii) rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency head designation to sign certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency heads may designate another person to sign certifications on their behalf; the designation must be in writing, signed by the agency head, and filed with the Department of State Miscellaneous Records Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation may be a letter or more formal document and should be mailed or hand-delivered to the Miscellaneous Records Bureau at One Commerce Plaza, Suite 600, Albany, NY 12231-0001, during specified hours. Provide the designation in advance of any filings requiring the designee’s signature.
